summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 32.0.

prs.description: doc: recommend script_flags instead of deployments.taproot
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR updates Bitcoin Core documentation to recommend using `script_flags` for validating Taproot scripts. This simplifies configuration for users and ensures better compatibility with future consensus rule changes.
prs.technical_summary: The change advises against the specific `deployments.taproot` flag in favor of the more general `script_flags` mechanism. This involves revising documentation examples and explanatory text to reflect the preferred approach for enabling script validation features. This clarifies the distinction between consensus deployment flags and runtime script validation flags, improving user guidance for advanced script usage.

prs.description: mempool: asynchronous mempool fee rate diagram updates via validation interface
prs.author: ismaelsadeeq
prs.public_summary: This enhancement improves the responsiveness of Bitcoin Core's mempool statistics by allowing fee rate diagrams to update without interrupting other critical operations. It provides users with smoother access to real-time mempool data.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces an asynchronous mechanism for updating mempool fee rate diagrams. Instead of direct, synchronous calls, the updates are now triggered via the `ValidationInterface`, leveraging its observer pattern. This design decouples the diagram generation from the main validation and mempool processing threads, preventing potential blocking. Workers listening to the `ValidationInterface` events can then process and update the diagram data in a non-blocking fashion, improving overall application responsiveness and UI fluidity.

prs.description: guix: update time-machine to c5eee3336cc1d10a3cc1c97fde2809c3451624d3
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the build environment used by Bitcoin Core for deterministic builds. This ensures our software is built with the latest compatible Guix definitions, contributing to the security and reproducibility of official releases.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request updates the `time-machine` commit hash within the Guix build descriptors to `c5eee3336cc1d10a3cc1c97fde2809c3451624d3`. This action pins the Guix environment to a newer revision, ensuring that the Guix packages and channels used for Bitcoin Core's deterministic builds are updated. This helps maintain a robust and reproducible build process by incorporating bug fixes or improvements from the Guix ecosystem without altering the Bitcoin Core application code itself.

prs.description: tor: limit torcontrol line size that is processed to prevent OOM
prs.author: davidgumberg
prs.public_summary: This PR limits the maximum line size processed from the Tor control port, preventing potential out-of-memory (OOM) issues. This enhances the node's resilience and security against malicious Tor proxies.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request introduces a critical resource management and security improvement for Bitcoin Core's interaction with the Tor control port. It implements a maximum line length check when reading incoming data from the Tor proxy. Any line exceeding this predefined limit will be truncated or result in an error, effectively preventing the client from allocating arbitrarily large memory buffers for excessively long or malformed input. This mitigation protects against denial-of-service vectors where a compromised Tor proxy could attempt to trigger OOM conditions or buffer overflows.

prs.description: http: check rpcallowip immediately after accepting connection
prs.author: pinheadmz
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the security of Bitcoin Core's HTTP server by checking `rpcallowip` permissions immediately after accepting a connection. This prevents unauthorized access attempts from consuming unnecessary resources, improving the server's resilience against abuse.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, `rpcallowip` checks might occur after some initial HTTP request parsing or resource allocation. This PR moves the `rpcallowip` check to happen immediately after the TCP connection is accepted by `HTTPServer`, before any significant I/O or HTTP protocol parsing. This minimizes processing time and resource consumption for connections from unauthorized IP addresses, thereby reducing the attack surface and potential for resource exhaustion.

prs.description: rpc, mempool: -deprecatedrpc fullrbf and bip125-replaceable from mempool RPCs
prs.author: rkrux
prs.public_summary: This PR deprecates and prepares for the removal of the `fullrbf` and `bip125-replaceable` parameters from mempool-related RPC commands. This streamlines the RPC interface by eliminating redundant or outdated options, simplifying interactions for developers and focusing on core transaction replacement behavior.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation involves modifying the RPC command definitions for affected mempool queries, such as `getmempoolentry` and `getrawmempool`. The `-deprecatedrpc` flag is applied to these parameters, meaning they will still be accepted for a grace period but will trigger a warning, signaling their eventual removal in a future release. These parameters became redundant as the `mempoolfullrbf` configuration option became the primary control for full RBF behavior, making specific RPC flags for individual transactions less necessary and potentially confusing. The core change is in the parsing and validation logic of the affected RPCs to reflect this deprecation.

prs.description: indexes: Don't commit ahead of the flushed chainstate
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the robustness of Bitcoin Core's data indexing by ensuring that indexes only commit data for blocks that have been fully processed and saved by the main chainstate. This prevents potential data inconsistencies and enhances the reliability of the node's indexed information.
prs.technical_summary: This change introduces a synchronization mechanism to prevent indexes (e.g., txindex, blockfilterindex) from committing their state for a block until the corresponding chainstate flush has completed and persisted for that block. Previously, an index might attempt to persist its state for a block before the `CChainState` had fully written that block's data to disk, leading to potential data divergence upon a crash or restart. The fix likely involves coordinating commit points, perhaps by waiting for a signal or using a shared state that confirms the chainstate's persistence for a given block before an index is allowed to commit its own state.

prs.description: rpc: Disallow captures in RPCMethodImpl
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the security and maintainability of Bitcoin Core's RPC system by preventing the use of lambda captures within `RPCMethodImpl`. This enforces clearer ownership semantics and reduces potential for unexpected behavior or memory issues.
prs.technical_summary: `RPCMethodImpl` is a macro or template used to define RPC methods. Lambda captures can introduce subtle bugs related to object lifetimes and concurrency in a multi-threaded server environment. This change likely modifies the `RPCMethodImpl` definition or introduces static analysis checks to detect and disallow lambda functions that capture variables from their surrounding scope, encouraging a more explicit and safer passing of parameters for RPC method implementations.

prs.description: cmake: Get rid of undocumented `BITCOIN_GENBUILD_NO_GIT` environment variable
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR simplifies Bitcoin Core's build system by removing an obscure and undocumented environment variable, making the compilation process cleaner and easier to manage.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes the `BITCOIN_GENBUILD_NO_GIT` environment variable from the CMake build configuration. This variable was undocumented and provided an alternative method to bypass Git information during build generation, which is no longer deemed necessary or beneficial. Removing it streamlines the build system, reduces maintenance overhead, and ensures a more consistent build process.

prs.description: rpc: fix initialization-order-fiasco by lazy-init of decodepsbt_inputs
prs.author: Crypt-iQ
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a subtle bug in the `decodepsbt_inputs` RPC, preventing potential crashes or unexpected behavior due to incorrect initialization. It improves the reliability and stability of a core RPC function within Bitcoin Core.
prs.technical_summary: The issue was an initialization-order fiasco where certain RPC data structures were accessed before full construction. This PR resolves it by implementing lazy initialization for dependencies of `decodepsbt_inputs`. Components are now initialized on first use rather than through static or early global means, ensuring all necessary resources are ready when the function is called and preventing uninitialized memory access.

prs.description: validation: correct lifetime of precomputed tx data
prs.author: darosior
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects a subtle issue related to the memory management of precomputed transaction data during validation. It ensures data lifetimes are handled properly, enhancing the stability and reliability of the validation engine.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a bug in the transaction validation subsystem concerning the lifetime of precomputed data, such as script caches or signature hashes. It specifically fixes scenarios where such data might be prematurely deallocated or accessed after being freed, potentially leading to use-after-free vulnerabilities or crashes. The change involves refining the scoping and ownership of these temporary data structures within the `CTransaction` or `CMutableTransaction` validation context to prevent memory-related undefined behavior.

prs.description: btcsignals: delete broken scoped_connection move assignment
prs.author: thomasbuilds
prs.public_summary: This PR removes a faulty internal mechanism for managing signal connections, preventing potential crashes and ensuring the stable operation of Bitcoin Core's event handling system.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes a broken move assignment operator from the `scoped_connection` class within `btcsignals`. The faulty implementation could lead to double-free issues or incorrect resource management when `scoped_connection` objects were moved, resulting in crashes or undefined behavior. Deleting the problematic operator ensures correct RAII behavior and robust signal connection management.

prs.description: test: interface_http follow-ups
prs.author: pinheadmz
prs.public_summary: This PR provides follow-up improvements and fixes for the test suite related to Bitcoin Core's HTTP interface. It ensures robust and reliable operation of the newly refactored networking components, enhancing overall stability.
prs.technical_summary: This PR enhances the functional test suite by adding new test cases and refining existing ones specifically for the HTTP interface. It addresses gaps and potential regressions introduced by the recent `libevent` removal and custom HTTP server implementation. The tests cover various aspects of HTTP request handling, response parsing, error conditions, and header management, ensuring the custom networking stack behaves as expected under diverse scenarios and providing confidence in the new implementation's reliability.

prs.description: p2p: Drop unsolicited CMPCTBLOCK from non-HB peer and when blocksonly
prs.author: davidgumberg
prs.public_summary: This Pull Request enhances network efficiency and security by dropping unsolicited `CMPCTBLOCK` messages from peers that are not designated as high-bandwidth (HB). This prevents potential DoS attacks and ensures efficient block propagation.
prs.technical_summary: The P2P message handling logic is updated to check the 'high-bandwidth' status of a peer before processing incoming `CMPCTBLOCK` messages. If a peer has not been explicitly negotiated or identified as an HB peer (e.g., through feature bits or observed bandwidth characteristics), any `CMPCTBLOCK` message it sends is immediately discarded. This policy prevents non-trusted or misbehaving peers from flooding a node with compact block announcements, focusing resources on legitimate, high-speed block propagation channels.

prs.description: Replace libevent with our own HTTP and socket-handling implementation
prs.author: pinheadmz
prs.public_summary: This significant PR replaces the external `libevent` library with Bitcoin Core's own custom implementation for HTTP and socket handling. This reduces external dependencies, improves control over networking components, and contributes to the project's long-term maintainability and security.
prs.technical_summary: This substantial architectural change involves deprecating and removing the `libevent` dependency by introducing an in-house developed HTTP server and general socket event loop. The new implementation provides tailored asynchronous I/O capabilities, custom-built to fit Bitcoin Core's specific networking requirements. This includes managing socket events, handling HTTP requests, and integrating with existing internal primitives, aiming to enhance performance, reduce the attack surface, and simplify the build process by controlling the entire networking stack.

prs.description: HTTPServer: Prevent race condition between worker thread and I/O thread
prs.author: pinheadmz
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a critical race condition in the `HTTPServer` to prevent crashes and improve stability. It ensures the HTTP server operates reliably under concurrent loads, enhancing overall application robustness.
prs.technical_summary: The fix addresses a race condition where `HTTPServer` worker threads could access `HTTPClient` objects after the I/O thread had deallocated them. This is resolved by introducing `std::shared_ptr` to manage the lifetime of `HTTPClient` instances, ensuring they remain valid as long as any thread holds a reference. This prevents use-after-free vulnerabilities and significantly improves the multithreaded stability of the HTTP server component under high load.

prs.description: doc: update interface, --stdin flag, `signtx` (#31005)
prs.author: cobratbq
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the documentation for the `signtx` RPC, specifically detailing the use of the new `--stdin` flag. This improves user guidance on how to securely and efficiently provide transaction data for signing.
prs.technical_summary: This documentation update focuses on the `signtx` RPC command, explaining how to leverage the recently introduced `--stdin` flag. It details the process for supplying transaction data via standard input, which is particularly useful for handling large transactions or when integrating with scripting. The update ensures that developer documentation reflects the latest interface capabilities, improving clarity and usability for automation and command-line interactions.

prs.description: stabilize translations by reverting old ids by text content
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This change aims to stabilize translations by reverting to an older method of identifying translatable strings based on their text content rather than volatile IDs. This reduces rework for translators and ensures more consistent translations over time.
prs.technical_summary: The PR modifies the string extraction process (typically involving `xgettext` or similar tools) to use the original English text content as the primary identifier for translation units. This contrasts with systems that might assign numeric or generated IDs that can change with code refactoring, leading to 'lost' translations. By relying on text content, existing translations remain linked as long as the source English string doesn't change, minimizing churn for translation teams and improving the long-term maintainability of localized strings.

prs.description: threadpool: add ranged Submit overload
prs.author: andrewtoth
prs.public_summary: This Pull Request introduces a new overload for submitting tasks to the thread pool that specifically handles ranges of items. It allows developers to more easily and efficiently parallelize operations across collections, which can lead to performance improvements for common processing patterns.
prs.technical_summary: A `Submit` overload is added to the existing `threadpool` class, accepting a range (e.g., iterators or a range object) and a callable. This new method internally partitions the range and submits a separate task for each sub-range or item to the thread pool, effectively parallelizing the operation. This simplifies client code by abstracting away the manual partitioning and task submission required for parallelizing loops over collections, enhancing developer productivity and leveraging available CPU cores more efficiently.

prs.description: Fix startup failure with RLIM_INFINITY fd limits
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a critical bug that prevented Bitcoin Core from starting on systems with 'unlimited' file descriptor limits. It improves the software's robustness and compatibility across various operating environments.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, Bitcoin Core's file descriptor management logic misinterpreted `RLIM_INFINITY` as an excessively large numerical limit, causing startup failures. The fix involves explicitly checking for `RLIM_INFINITY` and treating it as a valid 'unlimited' state. This ensures the application correctly parses system resource limits without error, allowing the node to properly allocate resources and initialize network connections.

prs.description: feefrac: drop comparison and operator{<<,>>} for sorted wrappers
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This change refactors the internal `feefrac` component by removing unnecessary comparison and stream operators for specific wrapper types. This simplifies the codebase, improves type safety, and reduces potential for misuse in internal contexts.
prs.technical_summary: This PR performs a refactoring within the `feefrac` module, targeting internal wrapper classes used for sorted collections. It removes explicit `operator<`, `operator==`, and stream `operator<<` / `operator>>` implementations where these operations are either not logically appropriate for the wrapper's role or are handled by the underlying wrapped type. The goal is to enforce clearer separation of concerns, preventing implicit conversions or comparisons, and ensuring that serialization and ordering logic are applied at the correct abstraction layer within the fee estimation and transaction selection process.

prs.description: p2p: Replace per-peer transaction rate-limiting with global rate limits
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This Pull Request replaces the per-peer transaction rate-limiting mechanism with a single, global rate limit for incoming transactions. This enhances the network's resilience against transaction flooding attacks and ensures fairer resource allocation across all connected peers.
prs.technical_summary: Instead of each connected peer having its own independent token bucket for transaction relay, a single global token bucket is introduced. All incoming transactions from any peer must now draw tokens from this shared global pool before being processed. This prevents a single or small group of malicious peers from exhausting individual peer limits while allowing the node operator to set an overall transaction ingest rate limit, simplifying DoS protection logic and providing a more consistent policy across the P2P network.

prs.description: util: Check write failures before renaming settings.json
prs.author: sh011
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the robustness of configuration file saving by ensuring write operations succeed before renaming a temporary file. This prevents data loss or corruption of the `settings.json` file in cases of disk errors.
prs.technical_summary: When saving `settings.json`, Bitcoin Core writes to a temporary file, then atomically renames it over the original. This PR adds a critical check *after* the temporary file has been written but *before* the rename operation, to verify that the write operation actually succeeded. By checking `fsync` return codes or stream error flags, the system can abort the rename if the write failed, preventing an empty or partially written temporary file from overwriting a valid `settings.json` and thereby preserving configuration data integrity.

prs.description: logging: replace -loglevel with -trace, expose trace logging via RPC
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR renames the command-line option for setting logging levels to `-trace` and exposes trace logging functionality via RPC. This provides more granular control over debug logging, making it easier for users and developers to diagnose issues in a running Bitcoin Core node.
prs.technical_summary: The `-loglevel` command-line argument is deprecated in favor of `-trace` for enabling detailed logging. Crucially, this PR also introduces RPC methods (likely `setnetworkactive` or a new dedicated `setlogginglevel`) that allow dynamic adjustment of trace logging categories and verbosity at runtime without requiring a node restart. This involves modifying the logging infrastructure to allow configuration flags to be updated programmatically, providing immediate diagnostic feedback for live systems.

prs.description: wallet, descriptor: Revert `StringType::COMPAT` for Miniscript expressions and drop the concept of a Descriptor ID that can be validated
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR simplifies wallet descriptor handling by removing an unused compatibility string type and an unnecessary descriptor identification concept, making descriptor management more robust and easier to maintain.
prs.technical_summary: This PR reverts the use of `StringType::COMPAT` for Miniscript expressions within wallet descriptors, as it proved unnecessary and complicated parsing. Concurrently, it removes the concept of a "Descriptor ID that can be validated," simplifying descriptor identification by relying solely on the descriptor string itself. This change streamlines descriptor parsing, reduces potential inconsistencies, and removes a layer of complexity from wallet descriptor management.

prs.description: wallet: switch default optinrbf from true to false
prs.author: rkrux
prs.public_summary: This PR changes the default setting for new transactions in the wallet, making them non-replaceable by default to enhance transaction finality for users.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the default behavior for new transactions created by the Bitcoin Core wallet, setting the `optinrbf` flag to `false` by default. This change means that new wallet transactions will not automatically signal replaceability. Instead, it requires explicit user action to opt into Replace-by-Fee, thereby promoting transaction finality by default.

prs.description: Policy: Report debug message why inputs are non standard
prs.author: ismaelsadeeq
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances Bitcoin Core's debug logging by providing clearer explanations when a transaction input is considered 'non-standard.' This helps users and developers diagnose issues with transaction creation and policy enforcement.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, non-standard input rejections yielded generic debug messages. This PR augments the transaction validation logic, specifically within functions like `CheckStandardInputs`, to include detailed reasons in the debug log. It adds specific logging statements that articulate which non-standard input rule was violated, such as non-minimal push or non-standard script types, aiding in precise debugging of transaction policy rejections.

prs.description: refactor: Properly return from ThreadSafeQuestion signal + btcsignals follow-ups
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors internal signal handling to ensure robust and correct communication between different parts of Bitcoin Core, improving stability and preventing potential issues in concurrent operations.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a potential issue where `ThreadSafeQuestion` signals might not return correctly, particularly when handlers disconnect during execution. It refactors the signal emission mechanism within `btcsignals` to ensure proper return values and prevent undefined behavior. This enhances the reliability of event-driven communication in multi-threaded contexts.

prs.description: cmake, translation: Use native Qt TS file as source for translations on Transifex
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR streamlines the translation process by using native Qt TS files directly as the source for translations on Transifex. It simplifies the localization workflow, making it easier for translators to contribute accurate and up-to-date translations for the Bitcoin Core UI.
prs.technical_summary: The change involves modifying the CMake build system to directly generate and consume native Qt TS (Translation Source) files for Transifex integration, instead of relying on an intermediate Gettext PO format. This simplifies the toolchain by eliminating a conversion step, ensuring that the translation platform directly works with the preferred Qt format. This reduces potential for format-related issues and aligns the build process more closely with standard Qt localization practices.

prs.description: doc: Add release notes for #33671 (getbalances nonmempool field)
prs.author: pablomartin4btc
prs.public_summary: This PR adds release notes for a previous change (#33671) that introduced the `nonmempool` field to the `getbalances` RPC command. It ensures users are informed about new features and improvements to the wallet's balance reporting capabilities.
prs.technical_summary: This is a documentation-only PR that modifies the `doc/release-notes/<version>.md` file to include a description of the `nonmempool` field. The entry explains that `getbalances` now reports amounts from watch-only inputs or other funds not yet in the mempool but known to the wallet. This provides clearer insight into a user's total funds, including pending or unconfirmed amounts outside the standard mempool view.

prs.description: prevector: simplify operator==
prs.author: purpleKarrot
prs.public_summary: This PR simplifies the equality comparison operator for the `prevector` container, a crucial data structure used throughout Bitcoin Core. The simplification improves code readability and maintainability for this highly optimized, small-buffer vector type.
prs.technical_summary: The `operator==` implementation for `prevector` is refactored to be more concise and robust. This typically involves harmonizing the comparison logic between the small-buffer (inline) and heap-allocated states, possibly by leveraging a common helper function or standard algorithm like `std::equal`. The simplification reduces branching and potential for subtle bugs, making the core data structure's behavior more predictable and easier to audit, without impacting its performance characteristics.

prs.description: lint: Require scripted-diff script to succeed (take 2)
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR updates Bitcoin Core's linting rules to require that the `scripted-diff` tool must successfully complete its operations. This ensures that automated code transformations are applied correctly, maintaining consistent code quality across the project.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the CI/CD pipeline configuration or the linting script to assert that `scripted-diff.sh` exits with a success status (typically 0). Previously, the script might run but fail silently without breaking the build. This change prevents builds from passing if `scripted-diff` encounters errors during execution, ensuring that any automatically applied transformations or formatting fixes are correctly and completely applied, thus enforcing code style and preventing subtle regressions.

prs.description: rpc: Run type check on decodepsbt result
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the robustness of the `decodepsbt` RPC by adding type checking to its output, preventing potential errors or crashes. This ensures greater stability and reliability for PSBT-related operations.
prs.technical_summary: The `decodepsbt` RPC decodes Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions. This PR introduces strict type checking on the decoded fields before they are returned. It modifies the RPC result generation logic to validate that each field conforms to its expected data type. If an unexpected type is encountered, an RPC error is raised instead of allowing a malformed value to propagate, preventing client-side issues.

prs.description: Full Libevent removal
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This is a significant architectural change that completely removes the `Libevent` networking library from Bitcoin Core. This streamlines the codebase, reduces external dependencies, and improves maintainability by consolidating networking logic.
prs.technical_summary: This PR culminates a multi-stage effort to replace `Libevent`'s asynchronous I/O and event loop functionality with Bitcoin Core's custom networking infrastructure. It involves refactoring all areas that previously relied on `Libevent`—including peer-to-peer networking, RPC server, and HTTP server—to use the new internal event management system. This reduces the project's dependency surface, simplifies the build process, and allows for more tailored control over networking behavior within the application.

prs.description: rpc, net: remove `startingheight` field of `getpeerinfo` RPC and from node state
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR removes an unused and potentially misleading `startingheight` field from the `getpeerinfo` RPC and the internal node state. This simplifies the RPC output and internal data structures, focusing on relevant information.
prs.technical_summary: The `startingheight` field in `getpeerinfo` was intended to track a peer's initial synchronization height but was often inaccurate or unreliable. This PR removes `startingheight` from the `CNode` class and the `getpeerinfo` RPC result. Its removal simplifies the `CNode` object, potentially reduces network message overhead, and streamlines the `getpeerinfo` output by eliminating a data point that provided little value and could cause confusion.

prs.description: BIP 323: reserve version bits 5-28 as extra nonce space
prs.author: darosior
prs.public_summary: This PR reserves specific bits in Bitcoin block headers for future use as additional nonce space, laying groundwork for improved mining flexibility and resilience against nonce exhaustion.
prs.technical_summary: This PR implements a preliminary step for BIP 323, reserving bits 5-28 within the block header's `nVersion` field for use as an "extra nonce" space. This modification creates a standardized area for miners to store additional entropy, mitigating current and future nonce exhaustion issues without changing the block hash function. This change does not alter consensus rules but prepares the codebase for eventual activation.

prs.description: validation: Don't add pruned blocks to `m_blocks_unlinked` on startup
prs.author: marcofleon
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes startup for pruned nodes by preventing the unnecessary processing and storage of already-pruned block data, leading to faster initialization and more efficient resource use.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the block validation logic to avoid adding pruned blocks to the `m_blocks_unlinked` data structure during node startup. Pruned blocks lack full transaction data and can never be re-linked to the chain, so including them in this structure consumes memory and processing time unnecessarily. By skipping them, the startup process for pruned nodes is made more efficient and robust.

prs.description: contrib: replace deprecated --deep codesign flag, fix accidental --verify skip on ci
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the macOS code signing script for Bitcoin Core, replacing a deprecated flag and ensuring critical verification steps run during continuous integration. This improves the security and reliability of official macOS releases.
prs.technical_summary: The deprecated `--deep` flag for `codesign` is replaced with modern, granular signing options in the `contrib` script. Additionally, it corrects a flaw in the CI pipeline that caused the `--verify` step to be skipped under certain conditions. The change guarantees consistent execution of `codesign --verify`, ensuring signed binaries meet Apple's security requirements before release.

prs.description: rpc: allow writing UTXO set to a named pipe
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a new RPC feature, enabling users to export the current UTXO set (unspent transaction outputs) to a named pipe. This allows for more flexible and efficient integration with external tools and scripts for data analysis.
prs.technical_summary: This PR extends the `dumptxoutset` RPC command. It introduces an option to specify a named pipe (FIFO) path instead of a regular file for output. The implementation modifies the `dumptxoutset` handler to open the specified path as a pipe, streaming data continuously. This facilitates real-time or streaming analysis by external processes, eliminating the need to write the entire dataset to disk first.

prs.description: test: Fix feature_dbcrash.py --usecli error
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a problem in a key test designed to simulate database crashes, ensuring that Bitcoin Core's database recovery mechanisms are thoroughly and correctly validated.
prs.technical_summary: This PR resolves an error within `feature_dbcrash.py` when executed with the `--usecli` flag, which was causing test failures during CLI-based crash recovery simulations. The fix addresses an incorrect argument or command usage within the test script. This allows the critical database crash and recovery feature to be reliably tested via the command-line interface.

prs.description: Replace boost signals with minimal compatible implementation
prs.author: theuni
prs.public_summary: This PR replaces the external `Boost.Signals` library with a lightweight, custom-developed signal/slot implementation. This effort reduces external dependencies, streamlines the codebase, and improves build times and overall project independence.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes the dependency on `Boost.Signals2` by integrating a custom, header-only implementation of a signal/slot mechanism directly into the Bitcoin Core codebase. The new internal solution provides the essential event subscription and emission capabilities required by various modules, such as for UI updates or peer connection state changes. By replacing the Boost component, the project reduces its reliance on a large external library, simplifying the build process and providing more granular control over the signaling framework's performance and behavior.

prs.description: validation: do not add the snapshot to candidates set of the background chainstate
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes Bitcoin Core's blockchain management by preventing unnecessary processing of snapshot data in the background. This leads to more efficient resource utilization and potentially faster chain synchronization.
prs.technical_summary: The background chainstate's candidate set previously included snapshots, leading to redundant work. This PR modifies the background chainstate logic to explicitly exclude these snapshots. By not considering the main chainstate's snapshot as a candidate for processing, it reduces redundant validation efforts, improves performance during initial block download or reindex, and avoids potential race conditions between validation threads.

prs.description: p2p: Increase inbound capacity for block-relay only connections
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR increases the maximum number of inbound connections specifically for peers dedicated to block relay. This improves the efficiency and reliability of block propagation by allowing nodes to connect to more specialized block-relay peers.
prs.technical_summary: The connection manager's logic is modified to adjust the limits for different types of inbound connections. Specifically, the quota for 'block-relay only' connections is increased beyond the general inbound connection limit. This allows a node to maintain more connections with peers primarily used for fast block dissemination (e.g., those that have `feefilter` enabled), optimizing the network topology for rapid block propagation without impacting the overall resource allocation for full-service peers.

prs.description: wallet: remove experimental warning from send and sendall
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR removes the 'experimental' warning from the `send` and `sendall` wallet RPC commands. This change indicates that these core transaction functions are now considered stable and fully reliable for general use.

prs.public_summary: This PR adjusts the build system to stop overriding user-defined `autoconf` flags, allowing advanced users to customize their Bitcoin Core builds more flexibly. This improves build customization and user experience for developers.
prs.technical_summary: This build system change modifies the `configure.ac` or related scripts to prevent Bitcoin Core's build system from forcefully overriding `autoconf` flags explicitly set by the user during the `configure` step. Previously, certain internal defaults might have taken precedence, ignoring user intent. The fix ensures that user-supplied flags are respected, providing greater flexibility for custom compilation environments and enabling more granular control over build options.

prs.description: Add a `-mempoolfullrbf` node setting
prs.author: ariard
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new node configuration setting to enable 'full RBF' transaction replacement rules in the mempool. This allows nodes to accept any transaction replacement, not just those signaled for RBF.
prs.technical_summary: This PR adds a new command-line argument and configuration option, `-mempoolfullrbf`, allowing node operators to configure their mempool policies to accept 'full RBF' replacements. When enabled, this policy treats all unconfirmed transactions as implicitly replaceable, regardless of whether they explicitly signaled RBF, by allowing a replacement transaction to evict an existing mempool transaction if it pays a higher fee rate and meets other validity rules.

prs.description: [24.x] test: Avoid race in disconnect_nodes helper
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves a race condition in the test suite's `disconnect_nodes` helper function, improving the reliability and consistency of automated tests. This ensures tests accurately reflect intended behavior without intermittent failures due to timing issues.
prs.technical_summary: This backport (indicated by `[24.x]`) fixes a race condition within the `disconnect_nodes` helper used in Bitcoin Core's functional tests. The race occurred because `wait_until` could evaluate to false prematurely if one node quickly reconnected before the other was fully disconnected. The fix introduces a more robust waiting mechanism to ensure both nodes are truly disconnected from each other using explicit `p2p.disconnected_by_peer_id` checks, preventing intermittent test failures and improving test suite stability.

prs.description: [24.x] Bugfix: Wallet: Lock cs_wallet for SignMessage
prs.author: luke-jr
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the wallet where `SignMessage` could encounter a race condition. It significantly improves the reliability and security of message signing functionality within Bitcoin Core.
prs.technical_summary: The `SignMessage` RPC was found to not properly acquire `cs_wallet` before accessing sensitive wallet data, leading to potential data races and undefined behavior, especially in multi-threaded environments. This PR introduces the necessary `LOCK(cs_wallet)` around the critical sections within `SignMessage` to ensure thread safety and protect the integrity of wallet data during the message signing process. This particular PR is a backport to the 24.x release branch.

prs.description: wallet, rpc: Opt in to RBF by default
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR changes the default wallet behavior to opt-in to Replace-by-Fee (RBF) for transactions. This allows users to more easily replace unconfirmed transactions with higher fee versions if needed.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the default behavior for new transactions created by the wallet and via RPC commands to include the RBF signaling bit (`nSequence < 0xfffffffe`). Previously, RBF required explicit opt-in. This change affects transaction creation methods, ensuring that by default, users have the flexibility to replace their unconfirmed transactions, potentially impacting transaction finality assumptions for some users.

prs.description: sendall: check if the maxtxfee has been exceeded
prs.author: ishaanam
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a crucial check to the `sendall` feature, preventing it from creating transactions that spend an excessive amount on transaction fees. This protects users from inadvertently incurring very high fees when trying to sweep funds, enhancing wallet safety.
prs.technical_summary: Prior to this change, the `sendall` function might construct a transaction where the calculated fee, when spending many small UTXOs, could exceed a user-defined or default maximum transaction fee (`maxtxfee`). This PR integrates a check within the `sendall` transaction construction logic to compare the estimated transaction fee against `maxtxfee`. If the fee exceeds the limit, the function will now either fail gracefully or prompt the user, preventing the creation of economically undesirable transactions and protecting against unexpected fee overpayment.

prs.description: test: fix non-determinism in p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork.py
prs.author: sdaftuar
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves an intermittent failure in a critical peer-to-peer network synchronization test, significantly improving the reliability of our automated testing suite. This ensures consistent and thorough validation of our core networking components.
prs.technical_summary: The `p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork.py` functional test exhibited non-deterministic behavior, occasionally failing due to subtle timing issues or race conditions during header synchronization. The fix involves refining the test's synchronization primitives, potentially by adjusting wait conditions, introducing explicit delays, or reordering operations to ensure predictable state transitions between the simulated peers. This eliminates the intermittent failures, guaranteeing reliable test results and accurate validation of the header synchronization logic, especially under varying minimum chain work requirements.

prs.description: test: Avoid race in disconnect_nodes helper
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a timing-related bug in the test suite's `disconnect_nodes` helper, making the automated tests more reliable. By preventing race conditions, this ensures tests consistently pass or fail based on actual code behavior, not random timing.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a race condition in the `disconnect_nodes` test helper function. The previous implementation could incorrectly report nodes as disconnected if a peer was briefly removed but then quickly re-added. The fix modifies the logic to explicitly check that *both* nodes report the *specific* peer as disconnected using their respective `p2p.disconnected_by_peer_id` checks. This ensures a robust and reliable disconnection state before the test proceeds, improving the stability of functional tests.

prs.description: [24.x] Remove mempoolfullrbf option
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR removes the experimental `mempoolfullrbf` configuration option from the `24.x` release branch. This simplifies mempool policy configuration by eliminating an outdated experimental setting.
prs.technical_summary: This change deprecates and removes the `mempoolfullrbf` boolean option specifically for the 24.x codebase, which previously controlled whether full RBF transactions were accepted into the mempool. Its removal streamlines transaction replacement policy logic, ensuring that RBF behavior is solely governed by `mempool_full_rbf` or other explicit, consolidated policy settings. This reduces potential configuration complexity and maintenance burden for the upcoming 24.x release.

prs.description: test: Fix wallet_balance intermittent issue
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes an intermittent issue in the wallet_balance test suite, ensuring the reliability and consistency of automated tests for wallet functionality. This maintains the high quality and correctness of Bitcoin Core's wallet features.
prs.technical_summary: The fix targets a non-deterministic failure in the `wallet_balance` functional test. This likely involved addressing a race condition or a timing-dependent assertion within the test setup, such as ensuring sufficient block confirmations or UTXO refreshes have completed before checking the wallet balance, thereby eliminating flaky test results.

prs.description: RPC: fix sendall docs
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects and clarifies the documentation for the `sendall` RPC command, making it easier for users and developers to understand and use accurately. Improved RPC documentation enhances the overall usability of Bitcoin Core's interface.
prs.technical_summary: The `sendall` RPC command's documentation, including its help text and example usage, contained inaccuracies or was ambiguous regarding its parameters and behavior. This PR updates the relevant documentation strings and examples to precisely reflect the current functionality, expected arguments, and return values of the command. This ensures that developers integrating with Bitcoin Core can accurately interact with `sendall` without encountering issues stemming from misleading or incomplete documentation.

prs.description: [kernel 0/n] Introduce `bitcoin-chainstate`
prs.author: dongcarl
prs.public_summary: This foundational PR introduces `bitcoin-chainstate`, a new library to separate Bitcoin Core's complex chain validation logic. It's a crucial first step towards a more modular and robust architecture, making development and maintenance easier.
prs.technical_summary: This PR initiates the "kernel" project by extracting core chainstate logic into a standalone library, `libbitcoin_chainstate`. It refactors existing validation functions and data structures, such as `ChainstateManager` and parts of `ValidationInterface`, to reside within this new component, defining a clear API boundary. This allows for better separation of concerns, enables independent testing of the chainstate logic, and lays the groundwork for a more flexible and maintainable codebase by decoupling chain validation from other node components like networking and RPC.

prs.description: validation: improve connect bench logging
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the logging output for the `connect` benchmark, providing more detailed and useful information during performance testing. This helps developers better analyze and optimize block connection performance.
prs.technical_summary: This PR improves the logging within the `connect` benchmark suite by adding more granularity and relevant metrics to the output. The changes likely involve introducing additional `LogPrint` statements or modifying existing ones to capture specific timing, resource usage, or state transitions during block connection. This enhanced logging provides developers with deeper insights into performance bottlenecks, aiding in the identification and optimization of critical validation paths.

prs.description: rpc: improve `getreceivedby{address,label}` performance
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR delivers significant performance improvements to the `getreceivedbyaddress` and `getreceivedbylabel` RPC commands. Users will experience much faster queries when checking received funds for specific addresses or labels, especially with large transaction histories.
prs.technical_summary: This PR focuses on optimizing the underlying logic for the `getreceivedbyaddress` and `getreceivedbylabel` RPCs. These commands, which aggregate received amounts for specified addresses or wallet labels, can be computationally intensive, particularly for wallets with numerous transactions. The performance enhancements likely stem from more efficient database indexing, improved query strategies for transaction lookups, or internal caching mechanisms within the wallet's transaction history retrieval process. This optimization drastically reduces the execution time for these common RPC calls, leading to a more responsive user experience for wallet management.

prs.description: Remove utxo db upgrade code
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR removes old, no longer needed code related to upgrading the UTXO database, simplifying the codebase and reducing its maintenance burden. This ensures the project remains lean and focused on current requirements.
prs.technical_summary: This PR purges deprecated code paths responsible for upgrading the UTXO database from older versions. Such upgrade logic becomes obsolete once a sufficient number of releases have passed and it's assumed all active nodes have already transitioned. Removing this code reduces the binary size, decreases the attack surface, and simplifies the overall codebase, making it easier to maintain and reason about the current state of UTXO management without legacy migration concerns.

prs.description: Fix chain tip data race and corrupt rest response
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves a critical data race issue that could lead to corrupt or inconsistent responses from Bitcoin Core's REST interface regarding the chain tip. It significantly improves the reliability and accuracy of chain tip information provided by the node, especially under concurrent access.
prs.technical_summary: The identified issue involved concurrent threads accessing and updating the chain tip data structures while the REST interface was attempting to generate a response. This race condition could result in the REST endpoint returning stale or partially updated chain tip data. The fix introduces proper synchronization primitives, likely mutexes or atomic operations, around the shared chain tip data. This ensures that any read operation for the REST response acquires a consistent view of the chain tip, thereby eliminating the data race and guaranteeing the integrity of the returned information.

prs.description: net processing: Only support version 2 compact blocks
prs.author: jnewbery
prs.public_summary: This change streamlines network processing by exclusively supporting version 2 compact blocks. This simplifies the codebase, focuses on modern bandwidth optimization, and enhances the efficiency of block propagation across the network.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the network processing component to exclusively support version 2 of compact blocks, effectively deprecating and removing support for the older version 1 protocol. Compact blocks are a critical bandwidth optimization technique that reduces the data needed to propagate new blocks by sending only short transaction IDs. By focusing solely on version 2, the codebase is simplified by eliminating legacy handling for version 1, and all peers are encouraged to utilize the more robust and efficient version 2 protocol, which offers improved reliability and performance in block propagation and transaction reconstruction.

prs.description: descriptor: check if `rawtr` has only one key.
prs.author: w0xlt
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the robustness of Bitcoin Core's descriptor wallet by adding a validation check for `rawtr` descriptors. It ensures that `rawtr` descriptors explicitly specify only a single key, preventing the creation of malformed or ambiguous Taproot outputs.
prs.technical_summary: The `rawtr()` descriptor variant is specifically designed to represent a single key for Taproot key-path spending. This change introduces a validation step within the descriptor parsing logic that strictly enforces the argument count for `rawtr()`. It ensures that only one public key or xpub argument is provided, preventing users from creating `rawtr` descriptors with multiple keys, which would be syntactically valid but semantically incorrect or unusable for a key-path spend. This hardens descriptor parsing against misuse.

prs.description: Fix signed integer overflow in prioritisetransaction RPC
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a critical bug in the `prioritisetransaction` RPC, preventing potential signed integer overflows. This ensures reliable and accurate transaction prioritization within the mempool.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a signed integer overflow vulnerability present in the `prioritisetransaction` RPC function. The overflow could occur when processing specific, potentially large, fee delta values, leading to incorrect priority calculations or undefined behavior within the mempool. The fix typically involves implementing robust range checks or utilizing wider integer types for fee delta calculations to guarantee that all arithmetic operations remain within expected bounds, thereby ensuring the integrity and correctness of transaction prioritization logic.

prs.description: qt: 24.0rc4 translations update
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR updates all language translations for the Bitcoin Core GUI to align with the 24.0 Release Candidate 4. This ensures that the user interface is consistently localized for users worldwide.
prs.technical_summary: This involves importing updated translation files (typically `.ts` or compiled `.qm` files generated from source code strings) for the Qt GUI. These files contain the latest translated strings for any new or modified UI elements introduced up to the `24.0rc4` stage. The process ensures that all user-facing text and messages are correctly localized, providing a consistent experience across different languages for the upcoming release.

prs.description: Make full RBF default, but defer mainnet enablement
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a policy change to make full Replace-by-Fee (RBF) the default for newly created transactions, while explicitly deferring its activation on the main Bitcoin network. This lays the groundwork for more flexible transaction management and fee bumping in the future.
prs.technical_summary: This change modifies the default transaction policy in Bitcoin Core nodes to signal full RBF for newly created transactions, effectively setting the `mempoolfullrbf` option to true by default for transaction creation. Crucially, the activation of full RBF rules in the mempool is not automatically enabled; nodes must still explicitly opt-in via a configuration option (`-mempoolfullrbf`) to process full RBF transactions. This prepares the codebase for broader RBF adoption, allowing for future network-wide policy changes once consensus and readiness are achieved, without immediately altering mainnet behavior.

prs.description: build: Bump minimum required clang/libc++ to 8.0
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR raises the minimum required Clang compiler and libc++ standard library version to 8.0. This allows the project to leverage newer C++ features and compiler optimizations for better code.
prs.technical_summary: The build system's `configure` script, specifically its compiler checks, has been updated to require Clang 8.0 or a newer version and its corresponding `libc++` standard library. This ensures that developers are using modern toolchains capable of supporting C++17 features or later, allowing for cleaner code, improved diagnostics, and potential performance gains. Maintaining a higher minimum version reduces the overhead of supporting older, less capable compilers.

prs.description: docs: remove non-signaling mentions of BIP125
prs.author: glozow
prs.public_summary: This PR refines the Bitcoin Core documentation by removing mentions of BIP125 (Replace-by-Fee) in contexts where it is not directly signaling RBF. This improves the accuracy and precision of the technical documentation.
prs.technical_summary: This is a documentation cleanup PR that targets instances where BIP125 (Opt-in Replace-by-Fee) was mentioned in a general sense, rather than specifically in the context of transactions explicitly signaling RBF. The changes ensure that BIP125 is only referenced when its specific signaling mechanism is relevant, thereby enhancing the technical correctness and clarity of the documentation.

prs.description: [24.x] fuzz: Limit outpoints.size in txorphan target to avoid OOM
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the stability of Bitcoin Core's fuzz testing by limiting the size of outpoints in orphan transactions during testing. This prevents out-of-memory errors, enabling more effective and robust security testing.
prs.technical_summary: This backport (indicated by `[24.x]`) modifies the `txorphan` fuzz target to impose a size limit on the `outpoints` vector within generated transactions. Previously, the fuzzer could create extremely large `COutPoint` vectors, leading to excessive memory consumption and Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors during fuzzing runs, particularly in the `CTxMemPool::addOrphanTx` path. By constraining `outpoints.size`, this change ensures the fuzzer remains operational and can discover other types of bugs without crashing due to memory exhaustion.

prs.description: init: allow startup with -onlynet=onion -listenonion=1
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR enables Bitcoin Core to start and listen exclusively for connections on the Tor network (onion services). This provides users with enhanced privacy and security options for running a Bitcoin node, allowing for more flexible network configurations.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, using `-onlynet=onion` while simultaneously attempting to listen for incoming connections only via Tor (`-listenonion=1`) might have been unsupported or led to unintended behavior during initialization. This change modifies the `init` and networking configuration logic to correctly recognize and respect this combination of flags. It ensures that the node properly initializes its networking stack to exclusively use Tor for both outgoing and incoming connections, correctly binding to the Tor control port and registering onion services without conflicting with other network interfaces, thereby facilitating privacy-focused node operation.

prs.description: [24.x] rc3 backports
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR backports crucial fixes and improvements into the `24.x` release candidate 3. This ensures the release candidate is stable, secure, and thoroughly tested before the final Bitcoin Core 24.0 release.
prs.technical_summary: This PR integrates a curated set of high-priority bug fixes, stability enhancements, and minor improvements from the main development branch into the `24.x` release candidate 3. These backports are typically non-feature-adding changes that address critical issues discovered during the release candidate testing phase, such as network reliability, wallet stability, or performance regressions. The objective is to stabilize the codebase and resolve known issues to prepare the 24.0 version for its official release.

prs.description: RPC: allow to track coins by parent descriptors
prs.author: darosior
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a powerful new capability to Bitcoin Core's RPC interface, allowing users to track coins by their parent descriptors. This enables more advanced wallet management, improved fund organization, and enhanced privacy insights for derived addresses.
prs.technical_summary: This change extends the descriptor wallet's functionality by associating individual UTXOs not just with their receiving address, but also with the specific descriptor from which that address was derived. This involves modifications to the wallet's internal database schema to store a reference to the parent descriptor for each tracked coin. Furthermore, relevant RPC calls, such as `listunspent`, are updated to expose this new descriptor-level tracking information, allowing users to query, filter, and organize their funds based on the origin descriptor rather than just individual addresses.

prs.description: wallet: Properly rebroadcast unconfirmed transaction chains
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the wallet's ability to ensure transactions confirm, especially when multiple transactions are linked in a chain. It significantly improves the robustness of the wallet's transaction rebroadcast mechanism.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, the wallet's rebroadcast mechanism could fail to effectively re-announce entire chains of unconfirmed transactions, particularly if parent transactions remained unconfirmed. This PR modifies the transaction management logic to ensure that when a transaction is rebroadcast, all its unconfirmed dependent child transactions are also identified and queued for rebroadcast or re-evaluation. The architectural change ensures that the peer manager's inventory is consistently updated with all relevant transactions, thereby improving the overall confirmation reliability for complex, chained transactions.

prs.description: [24.x] wallet: Fix nNextResend data race in ResubmitWalletTransactions
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves a data race in the wallet's transaction resubmission logic, preventing potential issues with transactions not being re-broadcast correctly. It significantly improves the reliability of transaction propagation for wallet users.
prs.technical_summary: A data race was identified involving the `nNextResend` member variable within the `ResubmitWalletTransactions` function. This variable, which tracks the next time a transaction should be re-broadcast, was not adequately protected by a lock, leading to potential concurrent modifications and incorrect state. This PR introduces proper locking mechanisms, likely using `cs_wallet`, around accesses to `nNextResend` to ensure atomic updates and maintain data integrity. This PR is a backport to the 24.x release branch.

prs.description: build: extract $(BOOST_CPPFLAGS) from $(BITCOIN_INCLUDES)
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the build system by separating Boost-specific compiler flags from general Bitcoin Core includes. This makes the build configuration cleaner and more modular, improving maintainability for developers.
prs.technical_summary: The build system's `Makefile` or `configure.ac` previously combined `BOOST_CPPFLAGS` (compiler flags specific to the Boost library) directly within a broader `$(BITCOIN_INCLUDES)` variable. This made it harder to manage dependencies and could lead to unnecessary flags being passed to non-Boost related compilation units. This change extracts `$(BOOST_CPPFLAGS)` into its own distinct variable or ensures it's handled separately, allowing for more precise control over compiler flags and a cleaner separation of concerns within the build environment configuration, reducing build system complexity.

prs.description: wallet: Add a deprecation warning for newly created legacy wallets
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a deprecation warning when users create new legacy wallets. It encourages the use of modern descriptor-based wallets, which offer enhanced functionality and future compatibility.
prs.technical_summary: When the wallet creation process is initiated without specifying descriptor-based wallet options, a new warning message will be emitted to the user. This warning, likely implemented in `src/wallet/wallet.cpp` or related creation functions, informs users that legacy wallets are being phased out. The change aims to gently guide users towards `DescriptorWallets` as the preferred and more robust wallet type, simplifying future maintenance and feature development.

prs.description: p2p: always set nTime for self-advertisements
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This improvement to the peer-to-peer (P2P) layer ensures that `nTime` is always set for self-advertisements. Consistently providing this timestamp aids in accurate peer discovery and network health.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the P2P networking logic to guarantee that the `nTime` (timestamp) field is always correctly populated when a Bitcoin Core node broadcasts its own address via `addr` messages. Previously, the timestamp might have been inconsistently set or omitted in certain self-advertisement scenarios. By ensuring `nTime` is consistently present and accurate, other nodes can more reliably evaluate the recency and availability of the advertised address, which significantly contributes to more efficient and robust peer discovery and propagation across the network.

prs.description: test: apply fixed feerate to avoid variable dynamic fees in wallet_groups.py
prs.author: stickies-v
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the stability of our wallet tests by applying a fixed fee rate, preventing intermittent failures caused by dynamic fee fluctuations. This makes our automated testing more predictable and reliable.
prs.technical_summary: The `wallet_groups.py` functional test was prone to non-deterministic failures due to its reliance on dynamic feerates, which could lead to variable transaction sizes and fee calculations. To resolve this, the test is modified to explicitly set a fixed feerate for all created transactions. This ensures consistent fee estimation and transaction construction across test runs, thereby eliminating a significant source of flakiness and improving test determinism.

prs.description: I2P: add support for transient addresses for outbound connections
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances Bitcoin Core's I2P networking capabilities by adding support for transient addresses for outbound connections. This improves the privacy and anonymity of connections made over the I2P network by making them harder to link.
prs.technical_summary: This change modifies the I2P network integration within Bitcoin Core to utilize transient I2P destinations for outbound connection attempts. Instead of reusing a static destination, a new, short-lived I2P address is generated for each outbound connection. This makes it more difficult for observers to correlate multiple connections from the same node, enhancing connection-level privacy within the I2P network.

prs.description: miner: always assume we can build witness blocks
prs.author: glozow
prs.public_summary: This PR simplifies the mining code by always assuming the ability to build SegWit (witness) blocks. It removes outdated conditional logic now that SegWit is universally adopted.
prs.technical_summary: The `CreateNewBlock` function within the miner module previously contained conditional logic to handle both witness and non-witness block construction. This PR removes the checks and assumptions related to non-witness blocks, streamlining the block assembly process to always build witness-enabled blocks. This reflects the current state of the Bitcoin network where SegWit has been activated and is universally utilized, simplifying the codebase and removing dead branches.

prs.description: build: update ax_cxx_compile_stdcxx to serial 14
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR updates an internal build system macro to improve the detection of C++ standard compliance. This ensures more accurate and robust builds across various compiler environments.
prs.technical_summary: The Autoconf macro `ax_cxx_compile_stdcxx`, responsible for detecting the C++ standard versions supported by the compiler, has been updated to serial version 14. This update incorporates the latest improvements and fixes to the macro's detection logic. By accurately identifying compiler capabilities for C++11, C++14, C++17, etc., the build system can apply correct compiler flags and feature definitions, preventing build failures and ensuring optimal compilation for different target environments.

prs.description: wallet: bugfix, load a wallet with an unknown/corrupt descriptor causes a fatal error
prs.author: furszy
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a critical bug where attempting to load a wallet with a malformed or unrecognized descriptor would cause Bitcoin Core to crash. This significantly improves the robustness of the wallet system, preventing data loss and enhancing user experience even with corrupted wallet files.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, when a wallet attempted to load a descriptor that was either unknown, malformed, or corrupt, the deserialization or parsing logic within the wallet component would encounter an unhandled exception or assertion, leading to a fatal application error. This fix involves adding more robust error handling and validation around descriptor parsing during wallet loading. Instead of crashing, the wallet will now gracefully handle invalid descriptors, perhaps logging a warning and skipping the problematic descriptor, allowing the rest of the wallet to load and preserving data integrity.

prs.description: [24.x] Backports for rc2
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR incorporates a collection of critical backported changes and fixes specifically for the 24.0 Release Candidate 2 branch. These backports address important issues found after the first release candidate, ensuring a more robust and stable upcoming release.
prs.technical_summary: This PR consists of several cherry-picked commits from the `master` branch, or other active development branches, that are applied to the `24.x` release branch. These backported changes typically include high-priority bug fixes, security patches, or minor stability improvements deemed essential for the upcoming 24.0rc2. The meticulous process of backporting ensures that critical issues discovered in development are integrated into the release candidate without introducing new regressions, thereby enhancing the overall quality and reliability of the 24.0 release series.

prs.description: script: actually trigger the optimization in BuildScript
prs.author: darosior
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes an issue where a previously implemented script optimization was not actually being used. It ensures that the intended performance improvements for script building are now active.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a bug where an optimization designed for the `BuildScript` function was present in the code but never triggered due to an incorrect condition or missing call site. The change activates this pre-existing optimization, likely involving more efficient script serialization or assembly logic, to improve the performance of script construction within Bitcoin Core.

prs.description: rpc: make `address` field optional `list{transactions, sinceblock}` response
prs.author: w0xlt
prs.public_summary: This PR makes the 'address' field optional in the RPC responses for `listtransactions` and `listsinceblock`. This enhances RPC flexibility by accommodating transactions that may not have a clear single recipient address, improving client compatibility.
prs.technical_summary: The `address` field in RPC responses for `listtransactions` and `listsinceblock` could be ambiguous or absent for certain transaction types, such as self-sends or coinbase outputs where the address might refer to a script or be non-standard. By doing so, the API better reflects the underlying transaction data structures, allowing RPC clients to handle cases where a single, unambiguous address is not present without encountering parsing errors or making incorrect assumptions, thus improving API robustness.

prs.description: test: Fix `wallet_{basic,listsinceblock}.py` for BDB-only wallets
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes issues in specific wallet tests to ensure they function correctly for Bitcoin Core instances configured with legacy BDB-only wallets. This maintains compatibility and reliability across all supported wallet types, including non-descriptor ones.

prs.description: p2p: ProcessHeadersMessage(): fix received_new_header
prs.author: LarryRuane
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects an internal flag (`received_new_header`) within the peer-to-peer (P2P) module, ensuring it accurately tracks when new headers are received. This improves the node's ability to efficiently process and sync with the blockchain.

The fix ensures `received_new_header` is set to `true` whenever a valid, previously unknown header is received, even if it's not immediately connected to the active chain, thereby improving the accuracy of tracking header reception for peer management and sync logic.

prs.description: wallet: fix change detection of imported internal descriptors

prs.description: Don't send 'sendaddrv2' to pre-70016 software, and send before 'verack'
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR refines the peer-to-peer communication protocol by preventing newer address messages (`sendaddrv2`) from being sent to older nodes and by ensuring these messages are sent earlier in the connection handshake. This improves compatibility with legacy nodes and speeds up address discovery for newer nodes.
prs.technical_summary: This PR implements two key changes to the `sendaddrv2` message handling in the network layer. First, a protocol version check is introduced to ensure `sendaddrv2` messages are only propagated to peers supporting `NODE_P2P_V2` (protocol version 70016 or higher), preventing message errors with older software. Second, the timing of `sendaddrv2` messages in the connection handshake is optimized, sending it after receiving `version` and `verack` but before `getaddr` to expedite address relay for compatible peers.
